events.title: Flash Flood Warning
events.description: FFWPHI The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Northwestern Burlington County in southern New Jersey... Southeastern Bucks County in southeastern Pennsylvania... East Central Montgomery County in southeastern Pennsylvania... Northeastern Philadelphia County in southeastern Pennsylvania... * Until 730 PM EST. * At 327 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across portions of the warned area. Up to a 0.5 inch of rain has fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 2.5 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Philadelphia, Bensalem, Mount Laurel, Willingboro, Florence, Burlington, Bristol, Mount Holly, Riverside, Hatboro, Beverly and Yardley.

location.region: Burlington, NJ; Bucks, PA; Montgomery, PA; Philadelphia, PA

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

5000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 10 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds could cause
downed tree branches, localized power outages, and reduced
visibilities.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet Friday, dropping
to 5500 to 6000 feet Saturday morning. Heaviest snowfall expected
late Friday morning into the overnight hours. Light flurries to 2
inches possible down to 5000 feet with higher accumulations
remaining above 6000 feet. Lull in activity Saturday afternoon
through Sunday, followed by additional snow Sunday night through
Monday.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet expected in the surf zone. Dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...North facing reefs of the Marianas. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM ChST Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An elevated, long-period north swell is producing hazardous surf up to 9 feet and a high risk of rip currents along north-facing reefs. Observation sites have reported surf up to 7 feet with frequent, larger sets of 7 to 9 feet already occurring along some north-facing reefs. Swimming conditions will be dangerous at least through late tonight before surf falls below hazardous levels of 9 feet shortly afterwards.

location.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

Total snow accumulations from 2 to 10 inches. * WHERE...Kodiak Island Northeast. * WHEN...From 6 PM this evening to 6 PM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Heavy snow and rain on snow may create difficult travel conditions. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A compact storm will move southeast of Kodiak Island tonight and remain nearly stationary through Friday afternoon to evening. Slight deviations in the storm position to the east and west will cause snow levels to fluctuate between sea level and 400 ft in elevation. Kodiak city and the archipeligo to the north are most likely to mix with rain at times, resulting in total snow accumulations of 2 to 4 inches. If rain does not mix in, expect higher snow totals. Areas from Kodiak Airport to Women's Bay are more likely to maintain a northwest wind, resulting in colder temperatures, a lower likelihood of rain, and snow accumulations from 6 to 10 inches.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night. Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at elevations of 2,500 feet, mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160 near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.

weather.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for Indiana can be obtained at https://511in.org.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

During lake effect snow, the weather can vary from bands of locally
heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away. Visibilities can
also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in weather,
visibility, and road conditions.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Tillamook County Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition, the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook River.

location.region: Tillamook County Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 10:22AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous
surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Tillamook County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately
10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically
results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook
River.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft Friday, increasing to 30 to 35 ft late Friday through Saturday. * WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Brookings. * WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 10 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas. Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Conditions may improve somewhat late Saturday as breaking wave heights lower to 24 to 27 ft, but another large ocean swell will maintain hazardous beach conditions much of the weekend and into Monday. * View the hazard area in detail at https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr

location.region: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast

and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties,piers, and other waterside infrastructure.

weather.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 4:52PM PST by NWS Spokane WA
weather.description:
* What...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups

* Where...Shoshone and Bonner Counties

* When...Until 11 AM PST Nov 13th

* Impacts...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.
weather.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor activity
during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air quality rule.
It is also recommended that all other individuals limit prolonged or
strenuous activity outdoors.

This statement is updated by the Idaho Department of Environmental
Quality, Air Quality Group. For more information contact DEQ's Coeur
d'Alene Regional Office at 208-769-1422.

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: * WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due to harmful levels of fine particle pollution. Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted air quality levels. * WHERE...in Vernon, Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne, Inglewood, Downtown LA, East LA and Huntington Park. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on emissions and local weather conditions. * WHEN...until 11:59 PM Thursday. * IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.

weather.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 11:29AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Vernon, Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne,
Inglewood, Downtown LA, East LA and Huntington Park. Levels of
particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
weather.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

Monday.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the
High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to
35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored
breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large
breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls,
inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur
Coast.

* WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from
midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide
is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49
PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the
Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea
walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.
weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From late tonight through late Saturday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Three to four and a half inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of the Olympics between early Friday and early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet.
